chunks: Al-Naḍr ibn Shuʿayb narrated from Khālid ibn Mādd, from al-Jāzī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who died and left behind a slave-girl, of whom he had freed one-third, then the executor married her before anything from the inheritance had been divided.

That she is to be appraised, and she and her husband are to work to pay the remainder of her price after she is appraised. So whatever befalls the woman of freedom or servitude applies likewise to her child.

key_terms.الْمِيرَاثِ: the inherited estate left by the deceased
key_terms.الْوَصِيُّ: the executor or trustee responsible for carrying out the bequest
key_terms.تُسْتَسْعَى: she is required to earn or work toward payment
key_terms.تُقَوَّمُ: she is appraised for her monetary value

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a partially freed slave-woman is married before the inheritance is divided?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a partially manumitted slave-woman who was married by the executor before the estate was distributed. The Imam عليه السلام rules that her value should be assessed and the remaining amount worked off, and that the legal status of her child follows her condition of freedom or servitude.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5496 - Al-Nadr ibn Shuayb narrated from Khalid ibn Maad from Al-Jazi from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding a man who passed away and left behind a slave woman of whom he had freed one-third. The executor of his will married her before any division of the inheritance had taken place.

Imam (as) said: "She should be appraised (for her full value), and both she and her husband must work to pay off the remaining value of her price after her appraisal. Whatever state - whether freedom or servitude - applies to the woman will also apply to her children."
